name: The shed on the strip between 1834 and 1900 Prairie Avenue (district draft; refined by T-1935)

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 0.250, v -3.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation -0.616 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1834-1900 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1834_1900 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading 'A narrow unnumbered strip between 1834 and 1900 (the block number "1" printed on it), unbuilt at the street, with a one-storey frame shed (yellow) at its alley end': 1 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: frame.

parts.from: s28fp-1834_1900-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 90% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1834_1900-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 90% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 713572318 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-west-2329.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads 'A narrow unnumbered strip between 1834 and 1900 (the block number "1" printed on it), unbuilt at the street, with a one-storey frame shed (yellow) at its alley end'. Backcast to 1904 as a yard outbuilding on the census ruling.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2329, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1935 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1834_1900-b1), the T-1841 census (s28-vacant-west-1834-1900) and the T-1837 register row none; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-west-2329).
